main_text.p: gantibus .Adde quod urinæ temperamen-to propemodum respondet, ac alterum ab altero tantum discrepat,quatum lac & fan-guis. At lac tanto frigidius sanguine esse, quató adenes, hepatis carne sunt frigidio-res,oftendit Galen. Comentario in Apho-rifmum quadragefimum,Sectionis quintę.

Propterea in hepatis substantia sanguis fit, in glandibus pectoris lac.Idcirco quemad-modum sanguis lacte paulo calidior est,ita & urina ipfo fero. Quoniam autem bilem flauam & aduftos humores benignè pur-gat(unde maniæ, melancholiæ, impetigi-ni,pruritui,lepræ,ulceribus malignis,febri-bus à bile putridis cœuenire fcribitur) ideo ipfum refrigerare,fed per accidens afferere audenter uelim. Igitur cuilibet elephantiæ fpeciei fuum debetur proprium catharti-cum,ut aduftæ & ulcerofæ ferum laftis,tu-berculofą[?] ueratrum nigrum,albę ueratrum album. Poftquam corpus leuatum eft eua-cuantibus,utendum eft exercitatione,præ-cipueq; curfu.Corpus enim calefacit,appe-titum proftratum reuocat, actiones natu-rales corroborat,ftomachum firmat, & de-fluxiones euocat. Etfi enim (inquit Oriba-fius ex Antylli fententia) curfus primum

page.notes: The initial word "tuberculosę" is hyphenated as "tu-" and continues as "berculofą"; the first letter of the continuation is not clearly visible and is marked [?]. The reading "albę" and "quató" are as printed, with the ligature/diacritic form uncertain. The printed line "gantibus" begins a fragment continued from the previous page. Printed forms such as "Comentario", "quód" spellings and "fanguis" are reproduced as printed.
